record.paper_title: Some open problems on well-filtered spaces and sober spaces
record.original_question: Is the product space of an arbitrary family of strong d-spaces again a strong d-space? A T0 space X is strong d if, for every directed set D in the specialization order, point x, and open set U, whenever the intersection over d in D of (up d intersect up x) is contained in U, some single up d intersect up x is already contained in U.

evidence.quote: Question 8.10. Is the product space of an arbitrary family of strong d-spaces again a strong d-space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be a T0 topological space, and let ≤ denote its specialization order (x ≤ y iff x belongs to the closure of {y}). For a point a ∈ X, write ↑a = {y ∈ X : a ≤ y}. Call X a strong d-space if, for every directed subset D ⊆ X (directed with respect to ≤), every point x ∈ X, and every open set U ⊆ X, the condition

  ⋂_{d ∈ D} (↑d ∩ ↑x) ⊆ U

implies that there exists some d ∈ D with ↑d ∩ ↑x ⊆ U.

Question: Is the topological product ∏_{i ∈ I} X_i of an arbitrary family {X_i}_{i ∈ I} of strong d-spaces (equipped with the product topology) again a strong d-space?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work appears to give a negative answer: two Scott spaces that are strongly well-filtered (and R-spaces, hence strong d-spaces) have been constructed whose product is not a strong d-space, resolving the question in the negative. This is reported as the main result of "Strongly well-filtered spaces and strong d-spaces" (Topology and its Applications, 2025), which states that it answers an open question of Lawson and Xu.

status_evidence.title: Strongly well-filtered spaces and strong d-spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Two Scott spaces which are strongly well-filtered and R-spaces have been given whose product space is not a strong d-space, which answers an open question posed by Lawson and Xu.
status_evidence.claim: The product of strong d-spaces need not be a strong d-space; a counterexample exists among Scott spaces.
